budget_items.what_was_said: Two board members reported two furniture quotes from the company that furnished the library, both coming in around the same total for tables, chairs, and lounge seating; the two options differed slightly in price depending on chair style.
The director's gift fund, made up of past donations to the senior center, covers most of the furniture cost, with revolving/formula grant money proposed to cover the remaining difference.

A board member recalled the town approving funding for a grant writer position roughly two years ago and said FinCom continues to ask for a concrete list of available grants before crediting savings from that position.

A board member asked how many residents might qualify for the 41A deferral, citing an income threshold for head-of-household eligibility, and noted deferred taxes are paid from the assessors' overlay/abatement reserve account.

A board member argued against eliminating a dietary aide position, citing the amount an aide relies on annually, and cautioned that eliminating a position through town meeting ties the board's hands versus simply shifting staff duties administratively.
As an example of a recurring grant opportunity, a board member cited a rebate the town receives per hybrid police cruiser purchased.
The director explained there is currently nothing budgeted for meals; the program is meant to be self-funding, with some meals costing more than charged and others less, roughly balancing out.

minutes.headline: Board informally opposed the town's move to mail-free warrants ahead of that night's town meeting vote
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging spent much of the meeting airing concerns—short of a formal vote—about the town's proposal to stop mailing warrants and go electronic-only, ahead of that evening's town meeting. Members also reviewed COA bylaw/charter language on hiring participation, approved new lobby furniture funded through the gift fund and grant money, agreed to a list of needs (assisted living, tax relief, parking, staffing, meals, walkability, programs) to send to the master plan committee, and heard a lengthy director's report on programs, trips, and the upcoming Festival of Trees and Christmas events.

what_happened.line: Members voiced opposition to the town's plan to stop mailing warrants and go electronic-only, without taking a formal vote, ahead of that night's town meeting.
The board agreed to send the master plan committee a list of senior needs covering assisted living, tax relief, parking, staffing, meals, walkability, and programs.
New lobby furniture was approved, to be paid mostly from the director's gift fund with grant money covering the remainder.
The board recommended adding positions to the personnel plan administratively rather than eliminating positions through the town meeting budget, to preserve flexibility.
Review of charter language on COA participation in hiring the center director was deferred pending more information from the select board and town manager.

why_it_matters: Ending mailed warrants would change how residents, including seniors without internet access, learn what is on a town meeting warrant.
The needs list submitted to the master plan committee can shape future town funding decisions on senior transportation, meals, facilities, and programming.
Whether staff changes go through administrative reclassification or a town meeting budget vote affects both the board's flexibility and job security for center employees.
watch_next: That evening's town meeting vote on electronic-only warrant distribution.
December 1 deadline for COA comments on hiring-participation charter language.
